features: HEADS UP — THIS VERSION CHANGES THE DATABASE (one migration). It adds the explicit link between an opening balance and the instalment plan that absorbed it, and it repairs affected installations on its own: balances left locked with no plan claiming them become editable again, balances legitimately in use stay protected, and supplier debts are left untouched.

Fixed — OPENING BALANCES STAYED LOCKED FOREVER. After creating an instalment plan that included the opening balances, using "Recalculate" (or removing an expense item from the plan) silently dropped those balances from the plan: from then on the plan covered the budget only, and deleting it no longer released the padlock. The balances stayed frozen — neither editable nor deletable — and no later plan would include them again. There was no way out from the interface.

Fixed — ARREARS COULD DISAPPEAR FROM THE INSTALMENTS WITHOUT SAYING SO. This is the accounting side of the same defect: after a recalculation the quotas no longer carried the previous debit or credit, so owners were charged the budget alone. A recalculation now keeps the balances that plan had absorbed, and the quotas stay identical to what they were before it.

The padlock on balances now has an owner: every locked balance records WHICH instalment plan absorbed it. It used to be a plain switch with no subject, so releasing it meant guessing after the fact by reading the generated instalments — the very information every recalculation erased. Deleting a plan now releases exactly the balances that plan was holding; those held by other plans stay protected.
Fixed: deleting an instalment plan also released previous supplier debts, which live in the same archive but never enter instalment plans. They are no longer touched.

Fixed: a plan created without "Generate the schedule now" locked the balances anyway, despite not containing them. The choice about balances is now recorded on the plan and read back when the instalments are actually generated, instead of being inferred from the state of the padlock.
Zero-value balances are no longer locked: they never entered an instalment plan, and they no longer show up in the allocation dialog during creation, where they were pure noise.

Fixed — A MANUAL SPLIT OF €250.00 CHARGED €25,000.00. A defect independent of the one above, present ever since manual allocation of joint balances (Art. 63) existed, and found while writing this version's tests: the amount entered was converted to cents twice, once by the controller and again by the generation step. One hundred times the amount due, on precisely the quota an administrator sets by hand because the automatic split doesn't fit. The automatic pro-rata split was never affected.

Fixed: the manual allocation of a joint balance disappeared at the first "Recalculate", silently replaced by the automatic pro-rata split. It is now stored on the plan and survives recalculations and the removal of expense items.

Fixed: an extraordinary plan generated later on pulled in the management's opening balances. The system claimed to ignore them, but only did so for plans generated immediately. An extraordinary plan now absorbs opening balances only when explicitly asked to.

When the data repair meets an ambiguous case — two plans of the same management both containing balance quotas, possible only in historical archives — it does not guess: it leaves the padlocks as they are and records it in the log. Better one padlock to open by hand than a double charge. Every repair decision is traced (management, outcome, plan, balances touched).

Thirteen new tests cover the whole reported path plus the guards that came out of reviewing the fix: a recalculation preserving both the balances and the manual split, a deletion releasing the padlock, a plan created without generation, an extraordinary plan leaving arrears alone, supplier debts left intact, removal of an expense item, and the automatic repair of already broken data (including the ambiguous case where it must stop).
